agent_trace.summary: On abdominal CT, the pancreas is normally a soft-tissue organ lying retroperitoneally behind the stomach and extending from the duodenum to the splenic hilum. It may appear abnormal if it is enlarged, surrounded by inflammatory fat stranding, has a mass, ductal dilation, calcifications, or reduced enhancement compared with the normal enhancing pancreatic parenchyma.

key_facts: The pancreas is normally fairly uniform in attenuation and enhancement on contrast CT.
Peripancreatic fat stranding is a common CT sign of inflammation.
Diffuse enlargement or focal contour change can suggest edema, inflammation, or a mass.
Pancreatic duct dilation or biliary dilation can be indirect signs of obstruction near the pancreas.
Calcifications within the pancreas are often associated with chronic pancreatitis.
